passages.text: That same day Jesus went out of the house and sat by the sea.
passages.sermon: Jesus left the house that day.\r\nHe went to the sea.\r\nHe sat by the sea.
passages.original: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν

passages.text: Such large crowds gathered around Him that He got into a boat and sat down, while all the people stood on the shore.
passages.sermon:
Jesus attracted many people.
Large crowds gathered around Jesus.
The crowds became so great that Jesus got into a boat.
Jesus sat down in the boat.
All the people stood on the shore.
passages.original: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει

passages.text: And He told them many things in parables, saying, “A farmer went out to sow his seed.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He used many parables.
He said, “Look.
A farmer went out to sow seed.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν

passages.text: And as he was sowing, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and devoured it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to a large crowd.
He told them a parable.
He said a farmer went out to sow seed.
As the farmer sowed, some seed fell along the path.
Birds came to the path.
The birds ate the seed on the path.
passages.original: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά

passages.text: Some fell on rocky ground, where it did not have much soil. It sprang up quickly because the soil was shallow.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people using parables.
He told a story about a farmer who sowed seed.
Some seed fell on rocky ground.
This rocky ground did not have much soil.
The seed on the rocky ground sprang up quickly.
The seed grew quickly because the soil was shallow.
passages.original: Ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς

passages.text: But when the sun rose, the seedlings were scorched, and they withered because they had no root.
passages.sermon:
The sun rose.
The seedlings were on rocky ground.
The seedlings had no root.
The sun scorched the seedlings.
The seedlings withered.
passages.original: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη

passages.text: Other seed fell among thorns, which grew up and choked the seedlings.
passages.sermon: Some seed fell among thorns.\r\nThe thorns grew up.\r\nThe thorns choked the seedlings.
passages.original: Ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἔπνιξαν αὐτά

passages.text: Still other seed fell on good soil and produced a crop—a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.
passages.sermon:
Some seed fell on good soil.
This soil was fertile.
The seed grew well in this soil.
The seed produced a crop.
Some plants produced one hundred times what was sown.
Some plants produced sixty times what was sown.
Some plants produced thirty times what was sown.
passages.original: Ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα

passages.text: He who has ears, let him hear.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people.\r\nJesus told them a parable.\r\nJesus said, “He who has ears should listen.”
passages.original: Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω

passages.text: Then the disciples came to Jesus and asked, “Why do You speak to the people in parables?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the people using parables.
The disciples followed Jesus.
The disciples came close to Jesus.
The disciples asked Jesus a question.
They said, “Why do you speak to the people in parables?”
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς

passages.text: He replied, “The knowledge of the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven has been given to you, but not to them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus answered their question.
Jesus said, “God has given you knowledge.
You can know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven.
God has not given this knowledge to others.
Others do not know these mysteries.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ὅτι Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται

passages.text: Whoever has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. Whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus explained a principle about receiving from God.
If a person has, God will give him more.
That person will have plenty.
If a person does not have, God will take away even what he has.
passages.original: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: This is why I speak to them in parables: ‘Though seeing, they do not see; though hearing, they do not hear or understand.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables.
He did this because the people saw, but they did not truly see.
They heard, but they did not truly hear.
They did not understand.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ Ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν Καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν

passages.text: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled: ‘You will be ever hearing but never understanding; you will be ever seeing but never perceiving.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people of Israel.
He explained why he used parables.
He said the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled in them.
God gave this prophecy through Isaiah.
The prophecy says, “You will hear with your ears, but you will not understand.”
The prophecy also says, “You will see with your eyes, but you will not perceive.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε Καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε

passages.text: For this people’s heart has grown callous; they hardly hear with their ears, and they have closed their eyes. Otherwise they might see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the people of Israel.
Their hearts have become hard.
They do not feel or care.
They barely listen with their ears.
They have shut their eyes.
They do not want to see with their eyes.
They do not want to hear with their ears.
They do not want to understand with their hearts.
If they did see with their eyes,
If they did hear with their ears,
If they did understand with their hearts,
They would turn back to God.
Then I would heal them.
passages.original: Ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου Καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν Καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν Μή‿ ποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς Καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν Καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν Καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν Καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς

passages.text: But blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He said their eyes are blessed.
Their eyes are blessed because they see.
He said their ears are blessed.
Their ears are blessed because they hear.
passages.original: Ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν

passages.text: For truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous men longed to see what you see but did not see it, and to hear what you hear but did not hear it.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
Jesus said, "I tell you the truth."
Many prophets lived before you.
Many righteous people lived before you.
They wanted to see what you see.
They did not see it.
They wanted to hear what you hear.
They did not hear it.
passages.original: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν

passages.text: Consider, then, the parable of the sower: When anyone hears the message of the kingdom but does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the seed sown along the path.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He explained the parable of the sower.
A sower spreads seed.
The seed is the message of the kingdom of God.
Some people hear this message.
They do not understand it.
The evil one comes to these people.
He takes away what was sown in their hearts.
This describes the seed sown along the path.
passages.original: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος Παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς

passages.text: The seed sown on rocky ground is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable about a sower.
The sower scattered seed on different kinds of ground.
Some seed fell on rocky ground.
This seed represents a person who hears the word of God.
This person receives the word immediately.
He receives it with joy.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν

passages.text: But since he has no root, he remains for only a season. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he quickly falls away.
passages.sermon:
This person hears the word of God.
He receives it with joy.
He has no root in himself.
He lasts only for a short time.
Trouble or persecution comes because of the word.
He quickly falls away.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται

passages.text: The seed sown among the thorns is the one who hears the word, but the worries of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
passages.sermon:
Jesus explained the meaning of the seed sown among the thorns.
This seed represents a person who hears the word.
The worries of this life affect this person.
The deceitfulness of wealth also affects this person.
These worries and deceitfulness choke the word.
The word becomes unfruitful in this person.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται

passages.text: But the seed sown on good soil is the one who hears the word and understands it. He indeed bears fruit and produces a crop—a hundredfold, sixtyfold, or thirtyfold.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about people who hear God's word.
Some people are like good soil.
The seed falls on this good soil.
This person hears the word.
This person understands the word.
This person produces fruit.
Sometimes he produces a hundred times what was sown.
Sometimes he produces sixty times.
Sometimes he produces thirty times.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα

passages.text: Jesus put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke another parable to the people.\r\nHe said, “The kingdom of heaven is like a man.\r\nThis man sowed good seed in his field.”
passages.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But while everyone was asleep, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat, and slipped away.
passages.sermon:
The enemy is a man who opposes the one who sowed good seed.
The enemy came while everyone was asleep.
He sowed weeds among the wheat.
He left after he sowed the weeds.
passages.original: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: When the wheat sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds also appeared.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable about the kingdom of heaven.
A man sowed good seed in his field.
The wheat grew and produced grain.
Weeds also appeared among the wheat.
passages.original: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια

passages.text: The owner’s servants came to him and said, ‘Sir, didn’t you sow good seed in your field? Where then did the weeds come from?’
passages.sermon:
The owner had servants.
The servants went to the owner.
They spoke to him.
They said, "Sir, you sowed good seed in your field."
They asked, "Where did the weeds come from?"
passages.original: Προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ Κύριε οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια

passages.text: ‘An enemy did this,’ he replied. So the servants asked him, ‘Do you want us to go and pull them up?’
passages.sermon:
The owner answered his servants.
He said, “An enemy did this.”
The servants spoke to the owner.
They asked, “Do you want us to go and pull up the weeds?”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτοῖς Ἐχθρὸς ἄνθρωπος τοῦτο ἐποίησεν Οἱ δὲ δοῦλοι αὐτῷ λέγουσιν Θέλεις οὖν ἀπελθόντες συλλέξωμεν αὐτά

passages.text: ‘No,’ he said, ‘if you pull the weeds now, you might uproot the wheat with them.
passages.sermon:
The owner answered his servants.
He said, "No."
He did not want them to pull up the weeds now.
He warned them.
If you pull up the weeds now, you might also pull up the wheat.
The wheat could be uprooted together with the weeds.
passages.original: Ὁ δέ φησιν Οὔ μή‿ ποτε συλλέγοντες τὰ ζιζάνια ἐκριζώσητε ἅμα αὐτοῖς τὸν σῖτον

passages.text: Let both grow together until the harvest. At that time I will tell the harvesters: First collect the weeds and tie them in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to his disciples.
He told them a parable about wheat and weeds.
He said, “Let both the wheat and the weeds grow together until the harvest.
When the harvest comes, I will speak to the harvesters.
I will say, ‘First, collect the weeds.
Tie the weeds in bundles to be burned.
Then, gather the wheat.
Bring the wheat into my barn.’”
passages.original: ἄφετε συναυξάνεσθαι ἀμφότερα ἕως τοῦ θερισμοῦ καὶ ἐν καιρῷ τοῦ θερισμοῦ ἐρῶ τοῖς θερισταῖς Συλλέξατε πρῶτον τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ δήσατε αὐτὰ εἰς δέσμας πρὸς τὸ κατακαῦσαι αὐτά τὸν δὲ σῖτον συναγάγετε εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην μου

passages.text: He put before them another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man planted in his field.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables.
He gave them another parable.
He said, “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed.
A man took this mustard seed.
He planted it in his field.”
passages.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν κόκκῳ σινάπεως ὃν λαβὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔσπειρεν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Although it is the smallest of all seeds, yet it grows into the largest of garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the air come and nest in its branches.”
passages.sermon:
The mustard seed is very small.
It is the smallest of all seeds.
A man plants this seed in his field.
The seed grows.
It becomes the largest of all garden plants.
It becomes a tree.
The tree is big and strong.
Birds of the air come to the tree.
The birds make their nests in its branches.
passages.original: ὃ μικρότερον μέν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων ὅταν δὲ αὐξηθῇ μεῖζον τῶν λαχάνων ἐστὶν καὶ γίνεται δένδρον ὥστε ἐλθεῖν τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ κατασκηνοῦν ἐν τοῖς κλάδοις αὐτοῦ

passages.text: He told them still another parable: “The kingdom of heaven is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables.
He told them another parable.
The kingdom of heaven is like leaven.
A woman took the leaven.
She mixed the leaven into three measures of flour.
She kept mixing until all the flour was leavened.
passages.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ζύμῃ ἣν λαβοῦσα γυνὴ ἐνέκρυψεν εἰς ἀλεύρου σάτα τρία ἕως οὗ ἐζυμώθη ὅλον

passages.text: Jesus spoke all these things to the crowds in parables. He did not tell them anything without using a parable.
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the crowds.\r\nHe used parables to teach them.\r\nHe did not speak to them without a parable.
passages.original: Ταῦτα πάντα ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν παραβολαῖς τοῖς ὄχλοις καὶ χωρὶς παραβολῆς οὐδὲν ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς

passages.text: So was fulfilled what was spoken through the prophet: “I will open My mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation of the world.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus fulfilled the words spoken by the prophet.
The prophet said, “I will open my mouth in parables.”
The prophet also said, “I will speak things hidden since the foundation of the world.”
Jesus spoke in parables to reveal these hidden things.
These things were hidden from the beginning of the world.
passages.original: ὅπως πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Ἀνοίξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὸ στόμα μου ἐρεύξομαι κεκρυμμένα ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου

passages.text: Then Jesus dismissed the crowds and went into the house. His disciples came to Him and said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus dismissed the crowds.
He went into the house.
His disciples came to Him.
They said, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
passages.original: Τότε ἀφεὶς τοὺς ὄχλους ἦλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ λέγοντες Διασάφησον ἡμῖν τὴν παραβολὴν τῶν ζιζανίων τοῦ ἀγροῦ

passages.text: He replied, “The One who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.
passages.sermon: Jesus answered His disciples.\r\nJesus is the Son of Man.\r\nThe Son of Man sows the good seed.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ὁ σπείρων τὸ καλὸν σπέρμα ἐστὶν ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου

passages.text: The field is the world, and the good seed represents the sons of the kingdom. The weeds are the sons of the evil one, and the enemy who sows them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the harvesters are angels.
passages.sermon:
The field is the world.
The good seed means the sons of the kingdom.
The weeds are the sons of the evil one.
The enemy who sows the weeds is the devil.
The harvest is the end of the age.
The harvesters are angels.
passages.original: ὁ δὲ ἀγρός ἐστιν ὁ κόσμος τὸ δὲ καλὸν σπέρμα οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τῆς βασιλείας τὰ δὲ ζιζάνιά εἰσιν οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ πονηροῦ ὁ δὲ ἐχθρὸς ὁ σπείρας αὐτά ἐστιν ὁ διάβολος ὁ δὲ θερισμὸς συντέλεια αἰῶνός ἐστιν οἱ δὲ θερισταὶ ἄγγελοί εἰσιν

passages.text: As the weeds are collected and burned in the fire, so will it be at the end of the age.
passages.sermon:
Jesus explained the meaning of the parable.
He said the weeds are collected together.
People burn the weeds in the fire.
The same thing will happen at the end of the age.
God will separate people at that time.
passages.original: Ὥσπερ οὖν συλλέγεται τὰ ζιζάνια καὶ πυρὶ κατακαίεται οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος

passages.text: The Son of Man will send out His angels, and they will weed out of His kingdom every cause of sin and all who practice lawlessness.
passages.sermon:
The Son of Man is Jesus.
Jesus will send out His angels.
The angels will go into His kingdom.
The angels will remove every cause of sin from His kingdom.
The angels will also remove all people who practice lawlessness from His kingdom.
passages.original: ἀποστελεῖ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τοὺς ἀγγέλους αὐτοῦ καὶ συλλέξουσιν ἐκ τῆς βασιλείας αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ σκάνδαλα καὶ τοὺς ποιοῦντας τὴν ἀνομίαν

passages.text: And they will throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
passages.sermon: The angels will throw them into the fiery furnace.\r\nIn that place, people will weep.\r\nPeople will gnash their teeth.
passages.original: καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων

passages.text: Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. He who has ears, let him hear.
passages.sermon:
The righteous will shine.
They will shine like the sun.
They will shine in the kingdom of their Father.
Anyone who has ears should listen.
passages.original: τότε οἱ δίκαιοι ἐκλάμψουσιν ὡς ὁ ἥλιος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ Πατρὸς αὐτῶν Ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω

passages.text: The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field. When a man found it, he hid it again, and in his joy he went and sold all he had and bought that field.
passages.sermon:
The kingdom of heaven is like treasure.
Someone hid this treasure in a field.
A man found the treasure.
He hid the treasure again.
He felt great joy.
He went away.
He sold everything he owned.
He bought that field.
passages.original: Ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν θησαυρῷ κεκρυμμένῳ ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ ὃν εὑρὼν ἄνθρωπος ἔκρυψεν καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς αὐτοῦ ὑπάγει καὶ πωλεῖ πάντα ὅσα ἔχει καὶ ἀγοράζει τὸν ἀγρὸν ἐκεῖνον

passages.text: Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls.
passages.sermon:
The kingdom of heaven is very valuable.
The kingdom of heaven is like a merchant.
This merchant looks for fine pearls.
The merchant searches carefully.
The merchant wants to find something precious.
passages.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ ἐμπόρῳ ζητοῦντι καλοὺς μαργαρίτας

passages.text: When he found one very precious pearl, he went away and sold all he had and bought it.
passages.sermon:
A merchant searched for fine pearls.
He found one very precious pearl.
He went away.
He sold everything he had.
He bought the precious pearl.
passages.original: εὑρὼν δὲ ἕνα πολύτιμον μαργαρίτην ἀπελθὼν πέπρακεν πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν καὶ ἠγόρασεν αὐτόν

passages.text: Once again, the kingdom of heaven is like a net that was cast into the sea and caught all kinds of fish.
passages.sermon:
The kingdom of heaven is like a net.
People throw this net into the sea.
The net gathers fish.
The net gathers every kind of fish.
passages.original: Πάλιν ὁμοία ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν σαγήνῃ βληθείσῃ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐκ παντὸς γένους συναγαγούσῃ

passages.text: When it was full, the men pulled it ashore. Then they sat down and sorted the good fish into containers, but threw the bad away.
passages.sermon:
The net became full.
The men pulled the net onto the shore.
The men sat down.
They sorted the fish.
They put the good fish into containers.
They threw the bad fish away.
passages.original: ἣν ὅτε ἐπληρώθη ἀναβιβάσαντες ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν καὶ καθίσαντες συνέλεξαν τὰ καλὰ εἰς ἄγγη τὰ δὲ σαπρὰ ἔξω ἔβαλον

passages.text: So will it be at the end of the age: The angels will come and separate the wicked from the righteous, and throw them into the fiery furnace, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
passages.sermon:
At the end of the age, God will judge all people.
The angels will come.
The angels will separate the wicked from the righteous.
The angels will throw the wicked into the fiery furnace.
In that place, people will weep.
In that place, people will gnash their teeth.
passages.original: Οὕτως ἔσται ἐν τῇ συντελείᾳ τοῦ αἰῶνος ἐξελεύσονται οἱ ἄγγελοι καὶ ἀφοριοῦσιν τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκ μέσου τῶν δικαίων καὶ βαλοῦσιν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν κάμινον τοῦ πυρός ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων

passages.text: Have you understood all these things?” “Yes,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He asked them a question.
He said, “Have you understood all these things?”
The disciples answered Him.
They said, “Yes.”
passages.original: Συνήκατε ταῦτα πάντα Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Ναί

passages.text: Then He told them, “For this reason, every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner who brings out of his storeroom new treasures as well as old.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
He explained a truth about the kingdom of heaven.
A scribe is a person who studies and teaches the Scriptures.
A scribe who learns about the kingdom of heaven becomes like a homeowner.
This homeowner owns a storeroom filled with treasures.
He brings out treasures that are new.
He also brings out treasures that are old.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Διὰ τοῦτο πᾶς γραμματεὺς μαθητευθεὶς τῇ βασιλείᾳ τῶν οὐρανῶν ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδεσπότῃ ὅστις ἐκβάλλει ἐκ τοῦ θησαυροῦ αὐτοῦ καινὰ καὶ παλαιά

passages.text: When Jesus had finished these parables, He withdrew from that place.
passages.sermon: Jesus finished telling these parables.\r\nHe left that place.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὅτε ἐτέλεσεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὰς παραβολὰς ταύτας μετῆρεν ἐκεῖθεν

passages.text: Coming to His hometown, He taught the people in their synagogue, and they were astonished. “Where did this man get such wisdom and miraculous powers?” they asked.
passages.sermon:
Jesus came to His hometown.
He taught the people in their synagogue.
The people were astonished.
They asked, “Where did this man get such wisdom?”
They also asked, “Where did He get these miraculous powers?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθὼν εἰς τὴν πατρίδα αὐτοῦ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ αὐτῶν ὥστε ἐκπλήσσεσθαι αὐτοὺς καὶ λέγειν Πόθεν τούτῳ ἡ σοφία αὕτη καὶ αἱ δυνάμεις

passages.text: “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son? Isn’t His mother’s name Mary, and aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?
passages.sermon:
Jesus returned to His hometown.
The people knew Jesus and His family.
They said, “Isn’t this the carpenter’s son?”
They said, “Isn’t His mother called Mary?”
They said, “Aren’t His brothers James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas?”
passages.original: οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τοῦ τέκτονος υἱός οὐχ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ λέγεται Μαριὰμ καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ Ἰάκωβος καὶ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Σίμων καὶ Ἰούδας

passages.text: Aren’t all His sisters with us as well? Where then did this man get all these things?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus came to His hometown.
He taught the people in their synagogue.
The people were astonished.
They said, “Aren’t all His sisters with us?”
They also said, “Where did this man get all these things?”
passages.original: καὶ αἱ ἀδελφαὶ αὐτοῦ οὐχὶ πᾶσαι πρὸς ἡμᾶς εἰσιν πόθεν οὖν τούτῳ ταῦτα πάντα

passages.text: And they took offense at Him. But Jesus said to them, “Only in his hometown and in his own household is a prophet without honor.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus was in His hometown.
The people there knew His family.
They took offense at Jesus.
Jesus spoke to them.
He said, “A prophet is not honored in his hometown.
A prophet is not honored in his own household.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐσκανδαλίζοντο ἐν αὐτῷ Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐκ ἔστιν προφήτης ἄτιμος εἰ μὴ ἐν τῇ πατρίδι καὶ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: And He did not do many miracles there, because of their unbelief.
passages.sermon: Jesus was in His hometown.\r\nThe people there did not believe in Him.\r\nBecause of their unbelief, Jesus did not do many miracles there.
passages.original: καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν ἐκεῖ δυνάμεις πολλὰς διὰ τὴν ἀπιστίαν αὐτῶν
